GenerateMoveStateMachine.maps_to: __init__'s INITIAL pick (flyconid.py:41-44) + telegraph_next_move's RAND roll (flyconid.py:71-84), both through weighted_branch_pick (state_machine.py:47-59)
GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: THE bug class of this stream, and this port reads it correctly -- it is one of the two monsters the original weight-vs-cooldown fix repaired. Flyconid.cs:39-43 uses AddBranch overload #8 (`int cooldown, MoveRepeatType`) three times and overload #10 twice, so every integer is a COOLDOWN and every weight defaults to 1f: RAND = [V_SPORES cd 3, FRAIL_SPORES cd 2, SMASH cd 0], all CannotRepeat, in that ADD ORDER; INITIAL = [FRAIL_SPORES cd 2, SMASH], both CannotRepeat, weight 1. flyconid.py:26-27 encodes exactly that (_MOVES in add order, _COOLDOWN 3/2/0) and rolls over the full three-item vector every transition so the draw count cannot drift. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py branch`, seeds b01-b05, 40 turns each, reference machine built on the sim's own MonsterMoveStateMachine with the C# parameters): the emitted sequences agree turn for turn up to the point the REFERENCE MACHINERY raises -- see the deadlock guard.

guards.what: REACHABLE all-zero branch vector: after the log tail [V_SPORES, FRAIL_SPORES, SMASH] every RAND branch weighs 0, which is monster_state_machine G7 arm (b)'s input
guards.rationale: The PORT is faithful here and that is the finding. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py deadlock`): the state is reached on all five probe seeds (turn 3-23; e.g. seed b03 turn 3) and the tail is always [V_SPORES, FRAIL_SPORES, SMASH] -- V_SPORES is inside its cooldown 3, FRAIL_SPORES inside its cooldown 2, and SMASH is the last move so CannotRepeat zeroes it. C# RandomBranchState.GetNextState then does max = 0, ONE rng.NextFloat(0) draw, `0 - 0 <= 0` on the FIRST branch, and returns branch 0 = V_SPORES. The port's weighted_branch_pick does the identical thing: same single draw (observed: 1 draw consumed) and the same first item, 'V_SPORES'. Same observable, same stream position. CROSS-RECORD SIGNAL, reported not re-verdicted: monster_state_machine G7b is labelled DORMANT on a zero-weight fuzz of 82 MACHINES, and Flyconid is hand-rolled so that fuzz never covered it. Its dormancy therefore rests on Flyconid not being a MachineMonster; the sim machinery raises RuntimeError('No valid branch in RandomBranchState RAND') on this input (state_machine.py:182-183), observed in the same probe. Porting Flyconid onto MachineMonster -- the codebase's stated preferred convention -- would crash the run on ported act-1 content.

guards.what: Cooldown semantics: the port's window `self._log[-cd:] if cd > 0 else self._log[-1:]` (flyconid.py:79-81) vs C#'s cooldown early-return PLUS the CannotRepeat arm
guards.rationale: C# computes `allowed * GetWeight()` where CannotRepeat blocks iff the LAST logged move is this state, and then a separate cooldown check early-returns 0 iff the state is in the last `cooldown` IsMove entries (RandomBranchState.cs:142-165; monster_state_machine steps 19-20). For V_SPORES (cd 3) and FRAIL_SPORES (cd 2) the last-1 window is a subset of the cooldown window, so the cooldown subsumes CannotRepeat and the port's single `m in window` test is equivalent; for SMASH (cd 0) C# skips the cooldown entirely and the port falls back to `self._log[-1:]`, which is CannotRepeat exactly. Short logs behave the same on both sides (Python's negative slice and LINQ TakeLast both clamp).

guards.what: WHEN the port appends to its log (flyconid.py:68, at perform time) vs C# (at roll time, MonsterMoveStateMachine.cs:76-79)
guards.rationale: Different instant, identical content at the only moment that matters. C#'s StateLog at a roll holds every previously-rolled move including the one just performed; the port's _log at telegraph_next_move holds every performed move including the one just performed. Executed by the sequence diff above -- a one-entry offset would desynchronise the cooldown windows and show up within three turns, and does not.

guards.what: The INITIAL RandomBranchState is the machine's initial state, so the game rolls once at AfterCreatureAdded; the port rolls in __init__ (flyconid.py:42-44)
guards.rationale: monster_state_machine step 28: a machine whose initial state is a BRANCH starts with an EMPTY StateLog (branches are not loggable), and step 30's sticky rule does not fire because the initial state is not a move -- so the game really does draw once before the first turn. Both sides therefore consume exactly one MonsterAi float at creation, and both evaluate FRAIL_SPORES' cooldown 2 against an empty log (weight 1). Confirmed by the draw counts in the executed diff and by the pre-existing pin test/test_monster_branch_audit.py::TestPreviouslyFixedBugClassRegression::test_flyconid_draws_every_turn (verified present by grep).

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 3-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 49 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [47,49], observed [47,49], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 49 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
